brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Full hex bases piece:0,0,0 and piece:0,0,1 stacked at the same cell (levels 0 and 1), with half-w bases at (1,0,0) and (1,0,1) beside them, joint-bolted at both levels. check_build ok, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: For a workbench, at least two drawers
requirements.evidence: Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm): notch:0#0,1#notch1 at level 0 and notch:1#0,1#notch1 at level 1, each filling the empty cell (0,1) between the touching bases on its level.

requirements.requirement: Tower is suited to a workbench (mounting to the bench)
requirements.evidence: No bench-mounting or fixing part was added; the tower is a freestanding stack.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex storage tower with two notch drawers, one per storey. check_build passes with meshClash clear. The tower is freestanding; no bench mounting was added. Material and load suitability are not verified.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
